ANT|Jalese Gordon.bio: Jalese Gordon was born on 8th November 2001 and started sailing at the age of nine at the Antigua Yacht Club because she loved the idea of doing any sport associated with the water. A year later, she began to train competitively with the Optimist team, where she gained the opportunity to compete both regionally and internationally. She later moved to 4.7 and Laser Radial, where she not only competed but was also able to train at the World Sailing Clinic and secure a position to compete at Youth Worlds. Recently, she gained the opportunity to get the Olympic scholarship and compete in the Summer Olympics in Tokyo in 2021. Moving from competing in dinghy sailing to bigger boats has always been a dream of hers. She notes that she feels extremely lucky and honoured to be a part of the team. "It's so nice to have teammates that you grew up with because everyone has this form of respect for each other and the knowledge and experience we all bring. I’m super excited and cannot wait to compete with so many amazing sailors from around the world!" Jalese's position on the boat is offside trimmer, which is new to her, but she notes that it has been an amazing challenge.

ANT|Jules Mitchell.bio: At 28 years old, Jules has been racing in the Laser Class for over 10 years, competing in many international regattas, including 2 Youth Worlds and a European Championship. He was skipper of the Cork 1720 that won Antigua Sailing Week along with teammates Rocco Falcone and Louis Bavay. He is a sailmaker by trade, having recently taken on the role of sales director of North Sails Antigua.
res: XXIII Central American and the Caribbean Games Barranquilla 2018

ANT|Junella King.bio: Junella is 26 years old and an RYA-accredited instructor at the National Sailing Academy. She learned to sail at the academy and has also completed the RYA Day Skipper courses. She is a competitive sailor and passionate about teaching people to learn to sail.

ANT|Louis Bavay.bio: Louis is an ocean man experienced beyond his years, travelling the world to compete in numerous events with local Opti teammates from a young age. He progressed into the 29er Class as crew for Rocco Falcone and gained offshore experience sailing the Antigua to Bermuda Race and a transatlantic crossing on the 1938 Fife Classic ‘Mariella’.

ARG|Alejandro Colla.bio: Alejandro Colla is an americas cup and olympic sailor. He competed in the finn class in the 2004 olympics and he was a member of the +39 americas cup team in the 2007 cup in Valencia, Spain. He is a multiple world champion and has competed in the TP52 class for many years.
res: Gaastra - Campeonato del Mundo de TP52
Audi - Campeonato del Mundo TP52Audi - Campeonato del Mundo TP52

ARG|Diego Garay.bio: Born in La Plata, Argentina, he began sailing on his father’s boat before moving on to the Optimist class. He started racing keelboats at a young age, competing first in the J/24 class and later in various rating classes. After graduating with a degree in Philosophy, he worked as a teacher for several years before dedicating most of his career to professional sailing and boat management. Today, he primarily competes in the TP52, Maxi, and J/70 classes.

ARG|Gabriel Marino.bio: I was born on April 5, 1986, in Mar del Plata, Buenos Aires, Argentina. I started sailing in Optimist, Laser, and J24. During that period, I became the J24 South American Games champion in 1987. I participated in thirteen seasons of TP52 between 2007 and 2020 in the Audi Med Cup and the 52 Super Series. Throughout those years, I achieved two first-place finishes in TP52 World Championships in 2009 and 2015. I also secured the top spot in the annual TP52 circuit in 2012, 2015, 2017, and 2019 with the yacht Azurra.
res: Marina Real Juan Carlos I, ESP

ARG|German Panei.bio: German Panei es el argentino con más experiencia en la Clase RC44. Ha sido trimmer a bordo del Peninsula Pretroleum durante muchos años. Su conocimiento de la clase es y ha sido clave para ayudar al equipo argentino a mejorar, especialmente ayudando a los jóvenes regatistas del equipo.

ARG|Guillermo Parada.bio: Guillermo Parada is one of Argentina’s most experienced sailors. He has sailed in Optimist, Cadet, 470, Lightning and won several World and Pan American Championships. He has also participated as an athlete at the 1988 Olympic Games, and was involved in the 2007 America’s Cup. In addition, he was the helm of the Siemens at the Audi MedCup Circuit and won four times the 52 Super Series as the helm of the Azzurra team.

AUS|Annie Wilmot.bio: Annie competed wth Australia in Spain at the 2023 SSL Gold Cup. She returns to the team in a new role on the bow for SSL Austrailia. She combines her Team sailing with a 49erfx campaign alongside Laura Harding with the objective of competing in LA 2028. Annie Wilmot grew up sailing on Sydney Harbour. She excelled in her youth sailing, winning the 2016 Youth World Championship in the 29er, before progressing into the Olympic class of the 49erFX.

AUS|George Richardson.bio: George is new to the team. He brings a wealth of big boat experience and expertise in the Pit role.

AUS|John Bertrand.bio: He is a two-time Olympian in the Finn, achieving a Bronze Medal at the Montreal Olympics of 1976. Now often referred to simply as 'The Great Man', John Bertrand AO was the Skipper of Australia II when that crew wrestled away the Auld Mug from the New York Yacht Club after 132 years of dominance.|Now the Boxing Kangaroo, and to a lesser extent the blue skirt worn by Australia II whenever she was hauled out, remain very much front and center in the mind of the Captain. No doubt this is because of the scale of that crew's achievements, but also because of the very nature of the person.|Bertrand epitomizes both the famous Aussie 'Can Do' attitude, and never-failing sense of humor. Time with Bertrand is to be cherished, and there are always absolute pearls of wisdom on offer too. One such example is how faced with enormous gravity at 3:1 down, the Captain implored his crew to remove everything from their minds and just look at one race at a time. And for three more races they did just that!|Of course the Antipodeans are also known for owning a decent suspicion of brashness and desire to just get on with it. In olden times it might have been called larrikinism, whereas today it is given the more friendly term of fun loving. The tales of the Australia II crew running through the American squad, as they went about their morning run, are as entertaining as they are insightful.|Bertrand is the Chairman of the Sport Australia Hall of Fame, whose members are Australia's sporting royalty and still very actively involved in his beloved Etchells. He won his first of two World Championships in this highly competitive class in 2010, and then his second in 2016. The former was raced in Ireland with Andrew Palfrey and Tom Slingsby as crew. John has always been keen to help bring athletes on, which is one of the reasons he is still so much involved in sport to this day, but in 2010 after winning the Etchells Worlds with John, Slingsby would then go on to win the World Laser Championships, and also be anointed the World Rolex Sailor of the Year.

AUS|Laura Harding.bio: Laura is new to the Austrailan team. She will fill a role involving both trimming and strategy or tactics. She is combining Team sailing with a 49erfx compaign alongside Annie Wilmot in the lead up to LA 2028.

AUS|Mark Bulka.bio: Mark Bulka has been hooked on sailing since the age of five, always chasing the next race and challenge. Sailing the Finn set him on a path to master the sport, and he has since become a five-time World Champion with numerous Australian and international titles. His success spans classes including Finn, Contender, Etchells, A-Class Catamaran, SB20, and Sydney 38, reflecting decades of skill, dedication, and a lifelong passion for competitive sailing.

BRA|Alfredo Rovere.bio: With more than 30 years of experience in internationalc and ocean racing, Alfredo Rovere has great ambitions in the first edition of the SSL Gold Cup. Born in Buenos Aires, Argentina, the athlete has lived in Brazil since 2000 and obtained naturalization six years ago. In addition to dedicating himself to sailing, Rovere holds a degree in Business Administration, from IBMEC-RJ, and in Yacht Design, from the Westlawn Institute of Marine Technology, in the United States. The bowman will carry the number 1 on the back of his uniform.

BRA|Andre Fonseca.bio: Velejador de grande experiência em regatas de longa duração, ele representou o Brasil em três edições dos Jogos Olímpicos (Sydney, Atenas e Pequim) e competiu três vezes na Volvo Ocean Race

CHI|Andrés Ducasse.bio: Accurate and methodical. This is our grinder. This position requires strength and sensitivity to know when and how much power to put into the trim of the sails. With his capacity for analysis and observation, Andrés shines in this position. He started sailing Optimist at age 6, and at 10 he made his competition debut. Since then, he has had great successes, being 3 times national champion in different classes, J70 World Champion in the Corinthian category in 2021 and an excellent participation in the Rio 2016 Olympic Games. He is currently a helmsman at J70 and S40.
res: J/24 World Championship Annapolis,Pan American Games

CHI|Benjamin Grez.bio: I started sailing at the age of 5 in the Optimist, inspired by my older siblings. In this class, I achieved three national titles, a South American championship, and two top-ten finishes in the world (8th and 2nd). This success enabled me to gain support from the federation and private companies, allowing me to pursue my sports career more seriously and professionally. After the Optimist, I sailed for 3 years in the 420, securing three South American podiums (1st, 2nd, 2nd), a third-place finish in the ISAF Jr. World Championship, and a 3rd place in the Open World Championship. With this momentum, the Olympic dream was born, and I started sailing in the 470, achieving a second-place finish in South America and qualifying for the London 2012 Olympics at the age of 19, becoming the youngest sailor in that event with only one year of experience in the class. As I grew, I was no longer able to continue as a helmsman in the 470. After 2 years away from sailing, I returned with my older brother in an Olympic project in the 49er category, successfully qualifying for Rio 2016 and achieving two South American podiums (1st and 2nd). Following this, I actively participated in the national S40 circuit as a helmsman and tactician for 2 teams.

CHI|Felipe Robles.bio: Dynamic and restless, our helmsman started sailing in Dinghy boats, with great results. He began in the J-24 class as helmsman and tactician in different prominent teams, obtaining Pan American Odesur medals and outstanding participation in world championships. He has great technical dialogue and full confidence in the capabilities of his team.

CHI|Nicholas Robertson.bio: Vigilant and proactive. Our Pitman does not miss one. Because of his experience on different ships and positions, he is the ideal navigator for the Pitman position, as he is located in the nerve center of the ship. All the maneuvers pass through here (hoisting, lowering, giving the correct tension to each halyard according to the intensity of the wind, in addition to the rough ones). He has been sailing in Optimist since he was 8 years old, participating in South American, North American and World Championships. He continued to compete in 420, Snipe, Lightning, J24, J105, Soto40, Oceanicos (ORC, IRC) and J70, where he obtained podium finishes in several national, world, and South American championships. He also has experience in offshore regattas (Fasnet, Caribean 600 and Transatlantic Race). He is currently dedicated to sailing, mainly on J70, Lightning, Soto40 and J105. He is passionate and enjoys sailing (and life in general).

CHI|Pablo Lorca.bio: As a naval aviator he is brave, risky and determined. Our captain began his relationship with the sea in the navy, where he learned discipline and logistics. In addition to being a great bowman, he has managed to form several successful projects: female and mixed crew, as well as match racing championships and corporate regattas. His wide participation in international championships together with his enormous social skills, make him “the man” for the job.

CHI|Rodrigo Amunátegui.bio: Methodical and meticulous, our main trimmer takes care of the rig tuning. His “zen” personality contributes to keeping the team calm in and out of the water. From a family of sailors, he began early in IMS boats as a main trimmer on a 40ft boat and as helmsman on Lightning, J-24 and oceanic ships. He is currently a J-70 tactician and main trimmer in S-40.

CHI|Rodrigo Robles.bio: Friendly and relaxed on land, focused and competitive in the water. Our Headsail trimmer carries his sails very safely. He manages the trim of the jib (upwind) and the spinnaker (downwind). He is part of the boat's speed team and is responsible for making permanent adjustments to all controls, depending on wind and wave conditions. He started sailing Optimist at the age of 8. He went on to sail J70, J24, Laser, and S40, where he has been a strong performer, winning national championships in several of these categories. During the breaks between regattas, Rocco is the entertainment of the team, with his dances and his friendliness at all costs.

CHI|Sebastián Prieto.bio: Sebastián Prieto es un regatista competitivo que representa a Chile en la exigente flota de regatas de la clase J/70.

COL|Ana Sofia Bermudez.bio: Ana Sofia Bermudez is a Colombian sailor dedicated mainly to the sunfish class, where some of her notable results have been: two-time silver medalist at the 2022 and 2023 Central American Games, national women's sunfish champion, 3rd place in the 2022 junior world championship, and 4th place in the 2022 women's world championship. She also has experience sailing 420 and lightning. She compete 3 years in optimist, consistently ranking in the top 3 nationally.

COL|Andrey Quintero.bio: Olympic athlete in the ILCA class and sailing coach Andrey Quintero has over 20 years of experience in high-performance sailing, establishing himself as a leading figure in the ILCA class (formerly Laser). He has proudly represented his country at the Olympic Games in the ILCA class, and has competed in 15 ILCA World Championships and five Pan American Games. Among his most notable achievements is earning the title of World Sailing Vice Champion, a testament to his technical excellence and competitive consistency. In addition to dinghy sailing, Andrey has extensive offshore racing experience as a helmsman and tactician on yachts from 38 to 44 feet, providing leadership and strategic insight at sea. He is currently active both as a competitive sailor and coach, dedicated to developing the next generation of top-level sailors.

COL|Esteban Echavarria.bio: Esteban Echavarria is a competitive Snipe and Sunfish sailor from Colombia and a two-time Colombian Olympic Committee Athlete of the Year in Sailing. A Bolivarian Games champion in both classes and fourth-place finisher at the Toronto Pan American Games, he has represented Colombia on the international stage for over a decade. He began his career in the Optimist and Laser 4.7, winning events like the U.S. Midwinters and Buenos Aires Sailing Week.

COL|James Medina.bio: James Medina started sailing in the sunfish class at the age of 14, performing one of the best junior sailors in Colombia and continued his process in different classes such as the 420 class, being selected to represent Colombia in the World Sailing youth World Championships in 2021. In the snipe class, he has been a two-time national champion in 2023 and a bronze medalist in the 2023 National Games. He also won a silver medal in the 2024 National Youth Sunfish Games.

COL|Juan Camilo Bustos.bio: With over 30 years of experience in sailing, Juan Camilo Bustos has built a solid athletic career, competing in classes such as Sunfish, Lightning, and J24. He has achieved outstanding results and podium finishes in national championships, as well as in international events including World, South American, Pan American, Central American, North American, and Midwinters championships. His career has been recognized on multiple occasions for his exceptional performance.

COL|Juan Diego Chaves.bio: 21 years old, currently studying to be a Mechanical Engineer; Juan Diego has been sailing competitively in Colombia since he was 9 years old. He has achieved massive experience in the Optimist, ILCA and Lightning classes; participating in ILCA7 South Americans, CAC games, CAC beach games and Junior South Americans. In the Lightning class, he has participated in Junior North Americans, South Americans and Junior Worlds. However, he has proven to be a highly versatile sailor, competing and excelling in Snipe and Catalina Capri 22 national championships. He specializes in ILCA7, where he has been ranked top 3 for three years in a row, winning silver in 2023 National Games and bronze in 2024 Junior National Games.

COL|Juan Esteban Restrepo.bio: Juan Esteban Restrepo Vera|Colombian sailor with 18 years of experience, specializing in the Snipe, Sunfish, and ILCA classes. Notable achievements include a gold medal at the 2017 Bolivarian Games, multiple medals at the National Games, several National championship titles, and a fourth-place finish at the 2015 Pan American Games. Twice named Colombia’s Best Sailing Athlete (Altius Award, 2015 and 2017).

COL|Julian Ramirez.bio: Julian Ramirez Arango is a Colombian sailor with 20 years of experience, specializing in the Lightning, Snipe, and Sunfish classes. He began his career in Optimist, later competing in Sunfish and ILCA, where he earned the title of Sunfish Youth World Champion. Representing Colombia in multiple international events—including the Pan American Games and Bolivarian Games—he achieved notable success, such as a third-place finish at the Lightning South American Championship.

CUB|Darien Martinez Pimentel.bio: Darién Martínez Pimentel es entrenador cubano de vela y exregatista, graduado en Educación Física. Como atleta, ganó una medalla de plata en los Juegos Centroamericanos y del Caribe de 2006 y participó en los Juegos Panamericanos de 2007. Ha conquistado varios títulos nacionales y, como entrenador de la clase Snipe, ha guiado a sus regatistas a obtener medallas en los Juegos Centroamericanos y del Caribe y a alcanzar el cuarto lugar en los Juegos Panamericanos.

CUB|Dennier Infante Pupo.bio: Es miembro activo del Equipo Nacional de Vela de Cuba y cuenta con una amplia experiencia en competiciones internacionales de la clase Laser. Ha participado en los Juegos Centroamericanos y del Caribe de Barranquilla 2018, los Juegos Panamericanos de Lima 2019, el Campeonato Sudamericano de Laser en Paracas, Perú, en 2018, y el Campeonato Norteamericano de Laser en Vancouver, Canadá, en 2017. Es cuatro veces campeón nacional de Cuba en la clase Laser y ha obtenido múltiples medallas en la clase Optimist. Es graduado en Educación Física y Deportes.

CUB|Erika Leonor Ibañes Batista.bio: In 2026, Ibáñez Batista made a major international breakthrough by winning silver with veteran Snipe champion Nelido Manso López in the Mixed Snipe event at the Central American and Caribbean Games in Santo Domingo. The Cuban pair recorded four first-place and six second-place finishes across 12 races, finishing just behind Puerto Rico.

CUB|Jose Antonio Urbay Torna.bio: Octavio Calixto Lorenzo Valdés es un campeón cubano de vela y un experimentado regatista que representa a SSL Team Cuba en la SSL Gold Cup a bordo del SSL 47. Natural de Caibarién, es conocido principalmente por conquistar el único título mundial de Cuba en la clase Snipe, junto a Nelido Manso López, en el Campeonato Mundial de Snipe de 1999, celebrado en Murcia, España.

CUB|Nelido Manso Lopez.bio: Nelido Manso López was born on December 26, 1966, residing in Caibarien Villa Clara, a university graduate in sports and captain of the ship. His main sporting achievements were champion three times in Pan American Games, Central American, and world champion.

CUB|Oscar Peres Rosales.bio: Oscar Pérez Rosales cursa actualmente el cuarto año de la carrera de Educación Física. Es un atleta talentoso que ha conquistado en tres ocasiones el título del Campeonato Nacional Juvenil, demostrando su constancia y espíritu competitivo.

CUB|Ovaldo Padron Delgado.bio: Padrón Delgado represents the Cuban national sailing program’s blend of experienced competitors and developing talent, racing aboard the one-design SSL 47 in a high-level international team format. His participation supports Cuba’s effort to build continuity and pass competitive experience to the next generation of Cuban sailors.

CUB|Reinier Manso Garcia.bio: Reinier Manso García representa a la nueva generación de la vela cubana. Forma parte de un programa de vela cubano dirigido por el experimentado campeón de la clase Snipe, Nelido Manso López, quien fue capitán del SSL Team Cuba y lo llevó hasta las finales de la SSL Gold Cup en Gran Canaria en 2023. Su participación refleja el compromiso del equipo con la formación de jóvenes regatistas y la transmisión de la experiencia adquirida en competiciones internacionales a las futuras generaciones de la vela cubana.

CZE|David Kovarik.bio: I had my first sailing experience at the age of four in the Optimist class, followed by lake racing around Prague. In 2013, I also began competing in international regattas aboard the TBoat 730i (Centomiglia, Rund um, Trofeo di Gorla, etc.), serving as a helmsman, trimmer, and mainsail trimmer. Since 2017, I have focused exclusively on ORC racing aboard the M37 as a bowman.

CZE|Honza Daněk.bio: A sailor since the age of nine, he is a multiple national champion in the Cadet, 470, RS Vareo, and Melges 24 classes. He was Vice World Champion in the Fireball class in 2004 and took part in the Olympic campaign in the 470 class for the Athens 2004 Olympic Games.|Throughout his career, he has held various positions aboard different sailing boats, primarily as a skipper, tactician, and headsail trimmer. A passionate windsurfer and kitesurfer, he is currently enthusiastic about foiling.

CZE|Martin Trcka.bio: A former Laser sailor, Martin competed in the Olympic Games in Athens in 2004 and Beijing in 2008. He has extensive experience sailing on big boats, having taken part in regattas such as the Sydney-Hobart Race and the Tour de France à la Voile. He currently sails in the Melges 24 class and on other big boats.

CZE|Ondra Teply.bio: A former Finn sailor, currently competing in the ILCA 7 class, Ondrej is an experienced athlete with an impressive track record. In 2013, Ondrej switched to the Olympic Finn class, where he pursued his professional sailing career. After the Finn class was dropped from the Olympic programme, he switched to the ILCA 7. In the Finn class, he won the Junior World Championship and the U23 European Championship. Ondrej also has extensive experience sailing in the Star class, having been part of the 2018 SSL Finals in the Bahamas. He is currently campaigning for Paris 2024 in the ILCA 7 class and will play an important role in the Czech team.

CZE|Pavel Bobek.bio: He started sailing in the Optimist class at the age of nine and achieved numerous outstanding results in national and international competitions. He later moved on to the 420 class and then to the 470 class, in which he competed in two Olympic campaigns. During this period, he also won multiple national championship titles in team racing.|After retiring from Olympic sailing, he spent two years as a professional crew member in the Melges 24 class, serving as a tactician. During this time, he achieved second place at the European Championship.|Currently, he competes in the ORC class as a skipper or tactician and in the Czech Sailing League aboard a Melges 24 as a tactician.

CZE|Petr Fiala.bio: He has been sailing since the age of six, achieving numerous successes in both national and international regattas. In the SSL, Petr can draw on his experience as a helmsman in different classes, ranging from small dinghies to large boats, having secured numerous podium finishes at World and European Championships.

CZE|Sara Tkadlecova.bio: Sara started sailing at the age of six as a crew member in the Cadet class. As a junior, she sailed the 29er for two years, both as a helm and as a crew member. At the age of 17, she began her Olympic campaign for the Tokyo 2020 Olympic Games in the 49erFX class with Dominika Vaďurova. In the end, they narrowly missed out on qualification. Nowadays, she continues to sail the 49erFX full-time, working towards the Paris 2024 Olympic Games.

DEN|Jeppe Borch.bio: Jeppe Borch is one of the world’s leading match racing skippers, having consistently ranked among the top sailors on the World Match Racing Tour over the past several years. Alongside his match racing career, he has also achieved success in keelboat racing, winning both the Sailing Champions League (J/70) and the ORC World Championship in 2025.

DEN|Mads Christian Taatø.bio: I started sailing in the Optimist dinghy at the age of seven and progressed to two-person dinghies and smaller keelboats. Since then, I have sailed as a bowman on various larger boats, ranging from 21 to 65 feet. I have also won several Danish championships in keelboat classes, with my best result being a second-place finish in Class B at the 2023 ORC World Championship in Kiel.

ECU|Alfredo Ochoa.bio: Sailing since he was 5 years old, Alfredo has been an active sailor for more than 25 years. He started as an Optimist sailor, competing at several South American and World Championships. He also won the National Championship in Opti Team Racing. He has also sailed Lasers, 470, Sunfish, ORC and Lightning Class, where he has obtained three podium positions at the Lightning Class Southamerican Championship, and obtained the Southamerican Championship in 2019 with Julio Velez and Irene Suarez. Alfredo is currently sailing Lightning Class and ORC racing on board a Swan 45, performing as mainsail trimmer/tactician and occasional skippering.

ECU|Alisson Haon.bio: Started sailing in 2023 as crew for the Ecuadorian team for the Pan American Games. She got 5th at the Pan-American Games. Then, she won the South American championship in the Lightning Class, and one week later, she won the World Championship in the Lightning Class. Since then, she has established herself as an excellent crew member of the Ecuadorian team.

ECU|Irene Suarez.bio: Irene is better known as "Bebe" for being the youngest of the group. However, at a young age, she has achieved many national and international achievements. Being multiple national champion and, at the time, a South American champion in the lightning class. She has managed to receive the award for best female sailing athlete from the Ecuadorian Olympic Committee on more than 4 consecutive occasions.

ECU|John Birkett.bio: John started in the Optimist class in Salinas, where he has lived all his life and is the city where sailing is most practiced in Ecuador. He has more than 15 years of sailing and continued his career representing his country in several classes including 470, Laser, Lightning, Snipe and Sunfish, obtaining international titles at the junior and senior level. He has been national champion on multiple occasions and in different classes. A passionate sailor with a strong character who always seeks to give his best in the water.

ECU|Jonathan Martinetti.bio: Since he was 11 years old, he was a sailor starting in the Optimist class, achieving many national and international titles. He has been South American Optimist Champion, two times Sunfish World Champion, three times Junior World Champion in three different classes, Pan American Champion in Sunfish class in Toronto 2015, and some other awards in the South American Olympic Circuit. He is passionate about sailing, competition, and the sea.
res: International Lightning Class Youth World Championship

ECU|Juan Andres Santos.bio: Sailing Lightning since he was 10 years old as crew. Have sailed important championships as North Americans, World Championships, and South Americans representing Ecuador. He won a South American championship as a crew and has been second and third various times. He has represented the country in the Pan-American Games on three different occasions.

ESP|Alejandro Muscat.bio: Alejandro Muscat was a member of the Spanish Olympic team in the Laser and Finn classes from 2005 to 2021. In addition, throughout his career, he has combined his participation in Olympic sailing with cruising and match racing.

ESP|Alfredo Gonzalez.bio: He began his competitive sailing career at the Real Club Náutico de Arrecife, where one of his instructors was Aureliano Negrín. He initially competed in the Optimist and Cadet classes. After alternating between sailing and Ironman triathlon, he joined the Snipe class, where he finished as runner-up in the Spanish Youth Championship in 2004 and 2005. In 2004, he won his first international title, becoming the European Junior Snipe Champion in Trieste.

ESP|Aureliano \"Nano\" Negrín.bio: He started sailing in the Optimist class when he was 8 years old, but an illness kept him away from sailing until he was 18, when he began to achieve important sporting success in the Snipe class, in which he won the European championship in 1998, was Spanish champion five times, in 1998, 1999, 2001, 2002 and 2004, and in 1999 he came fourth in the world championship. He also won the Spanish Cup four times, in 1997, 1998, 1999 and 2000.

ESP|Javier De la Plaza.bio: He won a gold medal at the 2000 49er World Championships and two medals at the 49er European Championships: silver in 1999 and bronze in 2001. He also competed in the 2000 Sydney Olympics, finishing fourth in the 49er class alongside Santiago López-Vázquez. He currently competes in cruising, TP52, RC44, and ClubSwan sailing.

ESP|Jordi Xammar.bio: He is one of the sailors with the greatest projection of Spanish sailing. At 26, he already has an Olympics to his name, having competed in Rio 2016. He is twice world champion in the 420 and once in the 470, in the youth category. In the 470, he has achieved both a silver medal and a bronze medal in the absolute category in both the World and European Championships. He was skipper of the Spanish Impulse at the Youth America’s Cup in Bermuda.

EST|Aasav Kevin Melvin.bio: Kevin Melvin is a young developing sailor whose last years have been dedicated to learning different positions in the keelboat in order to be an irreplaceable crew member in any team in the future. The best result at the moment is 4th place at the ORC European Championship

EST|Ago Rebane.bio: Ago has been sailing for over 45 years. In the past decade, he has been crowned as the World Champion in the X-41 class in 2010 and in the Platu25 class in 2021. In addition, Ago has two silver medals from European Championships in match racing. All these results have been achieved in Mati Sepp’s team. In SSL Team Estonia, Ago’s position is the mainsail trimmer.

EST|Janno Hool.bio: Janno is a former Finn sailor who now collects medals in Mati Sepp’s team. His recent achievements include a gold medal at the Platu 25 World Championships in 2021, a bronze medal at the Platu25 World Championships in 2019. At European Championships in match racing in 2016 and 2018, Janno was awarded with a silver medal.

EST|Karl-Hannes Tagu.bio: In the past, Karl-Hannes spent a lot of time sailing on the ice in the winter, first with the Ice Optimist and later in the most popular DN iceboat class. A real icebreaker! As his father was a sailor and boat builder,|Karl-Hannes has also been involved in the technical development of offshore and keelboats since he was a child. Today, he is a 3-time European champion in offshore sailing.|He also often drives match races."
res: Tallin, Haven Kakumae Yacht Club, EST
Tallin, Haven Kakumae Yacht Club, EST
Pirita Harbour, TOP Yacht Club, EST

EST|Mati Sepp.bio: Mati is the dream tactician for every team. He is always among the top sailors in the ranking of world match racing, which makes him one of the best European match race sailors. Mati has the title of World Champion in the X-41 and the Platu 25 class, two silver medals from the European Championships match race and several other championship titles and medals in the X-99, X-35, Platu 25 and ORC classes.

EST|Peter Saraskin.bio: Peter has participated in two Olympic Games in the Laser class and came 7th at the World Championships. He also has extensive experience in the X-99 class as the holder of two silver medals and one bronze medal at the World Championships. Peter is definitely one of the most skilled trimmers on large yachts in Estonia, which makes him an invaluable asset for the team.
res: Open & Women's Laser Radial World Championship

FRA|Ange Delerce.bio: Ange Delerce est l’un des plus jeunes marins de l’équipe représentant la Nouvelle Génération. Ange a débuté en Optimist mais c’est en 420 qu’il affiche des résultats très prometteurs. Une médaille d’Argent aux Championnats du Monde 2021 en Italie suivi d’un titre européen et d’une première place au Championnat de France Junior Match Racing en 2022 le placent dans le top 10 du classement mondial français. Ces résultats lui ont permis d’être sélectionné en Team France pour participer à la Gold Cup où il occupera le poste de flotteur. Son rôle est d’aider toute personne de l’équipe qui rencontre un problème, il contribue à apporter une grande fluidité à l’équipage. Pour cela, il s’adapte facilement à toutes les situations et possède une grande mobilité sur le bateau.

FRA|Edouard Masse.bio: Edouard Masse is the bowman on board Team France. At the front of the boat, Edouard akka Doudou is in charge of the spinnaker and the mast. He is also helping the helmsman and tactician to gauge the line and distance to other boats during the start or other maneuvers. A rôle he is mastering to near perfection after 5 Tour de France and many seasons in IRC and TP 52.

FRA|Loïck Peyron.bio: Loïck Peyron's reputation is well established! King of Ocean Racing, he holds the Jules Verne Trophy, won the English Transat three times, the ORMA World Championship four times, the Transat Jacques-Vabre three times, the Barcelona World Race and the Route du Rhum as well as eight times the Clairefontaine trophy. After co-helming the Alinghy boat in 2010 for the 33rd America's Cup in Valencia, he campaigned for the 2013 America's Cup first with Energy Team and then with Artemis Racing.

GBR|Ian Williams.bio: The 43-year-old captain of SSL Team GBR is the most successful skipper on the international match racing circuit. The former lawyer turned professional sailor was the first British skipper to win the Match Racing World Championship and has gone on to make history winning the prestigious title a further five times. Recently he has proven he has lost none of his competitive edge winning two of the world's leading match racing events, the Congressional Cup and Argo Group Gold Cup in 2019.
res: Monsoon Cup - Alpari World Match Racing Tour 2015

GBR|Matt Cornwell.bio: Coming from the UK’s sailing hotspot of Lymington, Matt Cornwell is one of the UK’s most sought-after bowmen. Having cut his teeth with the GBR Challenge America’s Cup campaign in Auckland in 2003, Cornwell was with the French Areva Challenge in Valencia four years later before joining Team Origin and ultimately the INEOS Team UK America's Cup challenge.

GER|Erik Heil.bio: How to win two 49er World Championship medals within two months and almost dethrone the Olympic Champion, America’s Cup Defender and SSL Ranking’s leader Peter Burling? 49er helmsman Erik Heil from Berlin can tell you all about it. The 2016 Olympic Bronze medalist, together with his crew Thomas Plößel is going to help propel Team Germany to success.

GER|Frithjof Kleen.bio: Frithjof “Frida” Kleen discovered his love for the sport on Berlin’s famous Wannsee. He came sixth at the 2012 Olympics and collected a golden star for winning the 2014 Star World Championships. A European Champion in the Dragon and a World Champion in the Swan 45, Kleen’s strengths include an exemplary fighting spirit, motivational talent and a famous sense of humor. Someone once said “Frida” moves on a boat like an elf with the power of a heavyweight boxer. He will use all of his superpower to push Team Germany in the SSL Gold Cup.

GER|Markus Wieser.bio: A former number one in the world of Match Racing, Markus Wieser is one of the most successful German sailing pros. As helmsman and world class tactician he holds World Cup titles in many different classes from big boats to Dragon, from 5.5mR to Tempest. Because of his outstanding achievements, Wieser is a popular ambassador for well-known global corporations.

GRE|Afrodite Zegers.bio: Afrodite Zegers-de Kleine – Autobiographical Summary|I was born on 2 December 1991 in Athens, Greece, and moved to the Netherlands at the age of 19 due to family reasons. I hold both Greek and Dutch nationality, speak four languages, and live a life combining professional sport, law, music, and coaching. I am married to Rogier de Kleine, and we have two dogs, Senna and Charlie. I hold a Bachelor’s degree in Law from the University of Amsterdam (UvA) and a Master’s in Criminal Law with a specialization in Economic Criminal Law from the Open Universiteit. I currently work as a Change Manager in Financial Economic Crime – Transaction Monitoring at Rabobank in Utrecht. I am a certified Master Practitioner in Neuro-Linguistic Programming (NLP), applying communication and mindset coaching in both sport and professional settings. Alongside my legal and coaching work, I am an active classical pianist, having graduated from the Athens Conservatory at the age of 16, and I serve as Head Coach of the Optimist class at the DRCS Yacht Club in Switzerland. I have held the No. 1 world ranking (World Sailing) in the 470 class from 2017 to 2018, and have won national titles in both Greece and the Netherlands. 🏅 Sailing Career Highlights I began sailing at the age of 9, and have represented both the Netherlands and Greece in top-level international competitions, including two Olympic Games:

GRE|Aimilios Papathanasiou.bio: A sailing athlete with 40 years of experience at the highest level, consistently representing the Greek National Sailing Team.|I have participated in five Olympic Games (four times in the Finn class and once in the Star class), achieving a best result of 5th place.|Throughout my career, I have won 5 medals at World Championships and 8 medals at European Championships, and reached the World No. 1 ranking twice.|One of the most meaningful distinctions of my career was receiving the IOC World Fair Play Award, recognizing the values ​​of sportsmanship, respect, and fair competition.|Beyond my athletic career, I have extensive experience in sports administration, having served as a board member and General Manager in major sports organizations.

GRE|Antonios Bougiouris.bio: I was born in Ermoupoli of Syros island on 1974|I gratuated from the national academy of physical education and sport science with bsc in sailing training category A|I currently.serve the coast guard as a navy commander where i was placed from the government due to my high level sports achievements.|I got touched with sailing at the age of 9,at Syros island and im in the national Greek sailing team 30 Years in classes Laser radial,laser stantard,tornado,ilca master,ilca mens,|I participate at sidney olympics 2000 and the preolympics of Atlanta 1996,sidney 2000,Athens2004,London 2012

GRE|Athanasios Chatzinikolidakis.bio: Born in Piraeus in 1955 Tasos Boudouris first stepped into a sailboat at the age of 3. He passed from Optimist to Finn, Laser, Soling, Star, Windsurf, 49er and competed 6 times in the Olympics placing 3rd in 1980 in Mosca (Tallinn). He holds the record (along with 3 others) for the most olympic runs as a Greek athlete. He is considered a pioneer of Greek sailing. He is also the president of the world olympians.

GRE|Chrysa Marinou.bio: From a young age, I was drawn to the sea. My father windsurfed, so I naturally tried to follow in his footsteps. I quickly transitioned to dinghies, starting with Optimists and then moving on to 420s. Nowadays, I train adults, form teams, and race together in Platus—an experience that has deepened my understanding of sailing theory and physics, and taught me how to effectively pass that knowledge on to others.

GRE|Stylianos Noutsos.bio: Born in Athens in 1982. Graduated the University of Correlco in Computer Science. Started sailing at 12 years old in the Optimist class, and then moved on to 420, 470, 29er and finally in 49er. Multi-National champion is the Star class and top podium places in offshore races across Europe in the last 20 years.

HUN|Aron Nemeth.bio: After sailing in different Olympic classes and fuelled by his passion for the seas and oceans, Aron decided to move to Australia in 2003. He has since participated in major big boat events in the FARR40 and SYDNEY38 classes and worked on MAXIs and MINI MAXIs. Due to his international experience in these classes, he has the most knowledge in the team of boats like SSL47.

res: 45th International Balaton Sailing Week & National Championships,
Pata Boats - Finn Junior World Championship (Silver Cup)

HUN|Szabolcs Majthenyi.bio: Since his childhood, Szabolcs has raced in different classes, including Optimist, Cadet, and 470. However, since 1992 his full focus has been on his beloved “Flying Dutchman”, where he won 13 world and 5 European championships. Since 1997, he has also worked as a coach and he is currently the head coach of the Hungarian 470 Olympic team, preparing for Tokyo

HUN|Tomai Balazs.bio: Parallel to his Olympic campaign for the Rio Olympic games in the Laser class, (he qualified his nation, but due to unfortunate circumstances was unable to participate) Balazs got his degree in civil engineering. Even today, being an active and successful sailor in different non-Olympic classes, he also works as an engineer in major construction companies around the country

HUN|Zsombor Berecz.bio: Without any dispute, the captain is the best active sailor in Hungary, proven by his national (28 national championships won) and international results in both Laser and Finn classes, recognised also by its 22nd SSL ranking. Still an active Olympic class sailor today and hoping for the games in Tokyo and the survival of his beloved Finn as an Olympic class, the SSL Gold Cup is his first venture as team leader in big boats against the world’s best sailors. “

JPN|Ai Yoshida.bio: Few Japanese sailors can match Ai Yoshida's depth of international experience. A four-time Olympian, she finished fifth at Rio 2016 and seventh at Tokyo 2020, and became 470 World Champion in 2018. Her career also includes World Championship silver medals and Asian Games gold. As Team Japan's Tactician, Yoshida brings that wealth of experience to the heart of the team's decision-making. Reading the racecourse, anticipating change and making critical calls under pressure, she brings the judgement and competitive instinct developed through years of racing against the world's best. EXPERIENCE. JUDGEMENT. INSTINCT.

JPN|Eiichiro Hamazaki.bio: Eiichirou Hamazaki is a distinguished sailing athlete hailing from Japan, known for his exceptional leadership as the captain of the SSL Gold Cup team, Rising Sun Japan. His sailing journey has been marked by outstanding achievements, including impressive results in the All Japan Yacht Match Race Championship and the Ninomiya Cup Match. Furthermore, his participation in the Sydney Olympics in the 470 class showcased his remarkable skills and dedication to the sport on the global stage.
res: All Japan Yacht Match Race Championship

JPN|Hideki Wakayama.bio: Hideki Wakayama, born in Hiroshima City in 1970, began his sailing journey in Hiroshima in 1996. Turning professional in 2000, he joined the Kansai-based sailing team SLED in 2003, participating in domestic races and later expanding to the east coast of the United States. Wakayama's notable achievements include winning the 2006 Farr40 Class North American Championship and becoming the Rolex TP52 World Champion in 2021. Active in the TP52 class, he secured impressive overall positions from 2014 to 2023, including a 2nd place in the 2023 12M Class World Championship.

JPN|Norio Igei.bio: Norio Igei is a highly accomplished sailing athlete from Japan, renowned for his exceptional skills and dedication to the sport. With a remarkable track record, he has achieved the prestigious title of World Champion in the TP52 class, showcasing his prowess on the international sailing stage. His passion for sailing and commitment to excellence have made him a celebrated figure in the global sailing community.

KOR|Dajeong Kim.bio: Da-jung Kim is a national team sailor in the 470 class, consistently balancing training and competitions throughout her career. She aims to give her best in every race and is a dedicated athlete who always strives to perform at her best.

KOR|Jia Kim.bio: Jia Kim began sailing naturally by following her father, a national team sailing coach. She started in the Optimist class and developed into an ILCA 6 class sailor, proving her skills in single-handed events by winning multiple national championship titles. Later, she transitioned to the double-handed dinghy 470 class, gaining a wide range of sailing experience. As a national team athlete, she has consistently challenged herself on the international stage and earned a bronze medal at the most recent Asian Games.

KOR|Minje Lee.bio: My hometown is the beach, so I naturally like the sea, so I started sailing. I still think that the cool feeling of crossing the sea is a charm that I can't get enough of. I have won a silver medal and a gold medal in high school at the National Sports Festival, which is the most important competition in terms of major grades.

KOR|Seung Kim.bio: "I have liked the sea since I was young and so I spent a lot of time in the ocean naturally.|Then I found out about yachting and that's how I started to sail.|My accomplishments as a sailor include coming 3rd, 2nd, and 1st place in Nationals, which is the biggest event in Korea."

KOR|Siyou Sung.bio: Seong Siyu is a South Korean sailor competing in the ILCA 7 class. He has steadily built his race experience by consistently participating in both domestic and international competitions. Through the SSL Asia Qualifier, he aims to take another step forward and grow further with the goal of advancing onto the world stage.

KOR|Sungbin Son.bio: Sungbin Son was introduced to sailing at a young age at the encouragement of his father, a high school sailing coach. He quickly fell in love with the sport and worked hard to develop his skills. His dedication paid off when he won the gold medal in the Optimist class at the 2014 Incheon Asian Games.

KOR|Sunjin An.bio: Sungbin Son was introduced to sailing at a young age at the encouragement of his father, a high school sailing coach. He quickly fell in love with the sport and worked hard to develop his skills. His dedication paid off when he won the gold medal in the Optimist class at the 2014 Incheon Asian Games.

LTU|Andrius Ramonaitis.bio: Racing for almost 19 years, Andrius Ramonaitis has experience with many classes – starting from single-handed and double-handed Olympic classes, he later transitioned to one designs constructed for team sailing. He was on the first youth team in Lithuanian history to race in AF Offshore Race and now for several years has been the skipper in „RS-280“ class, which is one of the biggest one-design fleets in Lithuania.

LTU|Domantas Juškevičius.bio: Domantas Juškevičius has been sailing since 5 years old. In his sailing career - more that 200 regattas and championships with Optimist and ILCA sailing classes. For the past few years, however, he has been more focused on offshore sailing and has already gathered more than 20 000 nm with Volvo 65 class yacht Ambersail-2, took part in various prestigious regattas and even The Ocean Race Europe.

LTU|Emilis Valentinaitis.bio: Emilis Valentinaitis is one of the team's youngsters, who has been building his racing skills|for more than 10 years now. Started from 470, now he concentrates on team sailing with|various classes and already has quite substantial experience in sailing together with and even|against other team members. Strong focus and eagerness for constant improvement makes|him a great trimmer.

LTU|Gintarè Scheidt.bio: The captain of The Ambers came into sailing almost together with the freedom of her country. Growing as a high-class sailor in a newly reborn Lithuania, Gintarė Volungevičiūtė Scheidt represented her country with the highest sailing achievements so far – an Olympic silver medal in 2008, a gold at a World championship in 2012 and a huge hope and inspiration for future generations. Her positivity and motivation is what makes the team tick.
res: Audi - World Laser Radial Women's Championship

LTU|Karolis Janulionis.bio: A former member of Lithuanian ILCA national team and seven times Lithuanian ILCA 7 champion,|he has been successfully racing in various international ILCA 6 and ILCA 7 championships for many years now.|Parallelly, Karolis has been taking part in various ORC and one design team racing events.|Combined experience makes him a person who knows perfectly well how to synchronize|personal excellence and team responsibilities.
res: El Puerto de Santa Maria, Cadiz, ESP

LTU|Klaudio Kliučinskas.bio: Coming from a sailor's family, he has been in the midst of sailing since three months old. For the past few decades Klaudio has been racing in one-design and ORC events as well as a truly offshore sailing with Volvo60 in Sydney Hobart, Fastnet Race, Rolex Middle Sea Race, Caribbean 600 and others. His massive experience is a true treasure for our team.

LTU|Kristoforas Akromas.bio: Although he started sailing in his 20s, during the last seven years Kristoforas took part in almost all ORC World and ORC Europe events, as well as other regattas. His main strength lies not only in his team sailing skills but also in his persistence put all his efforts into enhancing the performance of the team as a whole.

LTU|Martin Volkovicki.bio: He started sailing in his teens and hasn't missed a season for 20 years now. Martin's specialty is team sailing, as he has competed in such yacht classes as J70, Evento42, X-35, RC44, Platu 25. As a bowman of The Ambers team, he not only takes care of everything that takes place on the bow of the yacht but also is an example of concentration and psychological stability in most stressful times.

LTU|Raimondas Šiugždinis.bio: European and World champion in ILCA 6 class and a keen sailor in various single-handed and team sailing one-designs – Raimondas Šiugždinis is considered to be one of the best Lithuanian helmsmen. His talent is supplemented by many years of experience in various ORC and one-design racing events, as well as some offshore challenges with Volvo60 and Volvo65. With him by the helm, the team will fight for the win until the last second.

MAS|Abdul Latif Mansor.bio: A rising star in Malaysian sailing, Latif is a two-time SEA Games medalist and one of the youngest athletes on the national team. Driven by incredible youthful energy and determination, he first made his mark in the Optimist class, where he won a SEA Games gold medal, before going on to achieve an impressive 11th-place finish at the 29er World Championships. A commando with an unwavering passion for sailing, Latif now competes actively across multiple keelboat classes and is set to represent Malaysia once again at the upcoming SEA Games as part of the SSL Team. Latif hails from Kuala Terengganu in the state of Terengganu
res: Royal Langkawi International Regatta. Malaysia. 2, 2024, Farr Platu, Royal Langkawi International Regatta
Platu Macth Racing, Royal Selangor Yacht Club

MAS|Ahmad Faizul Aswad Mohamed.bio: An old hand of Malaysian keelboat racing, he is now a professional sailing instructor. Aswad competed in the World Match Racing Tour (WMRT) with Malaysia's Koo Racing Team with their best ranking of 13th in the world in 2016. They came second in the 2016 WMRT USA Grand Slam Series, and has competed in the WMRT M32 series. A key crew member of Malaysia's sole TP52 Ulumulu and formerly of Hong Kong's Reichel/Pugh 77 Jelik, his keelboat experience lends crucial guidance to the team. He hails from Kuantan in the state of Pahang.
res: USA Grand Slam Series, World Match Racing Tour

MAS|Ahmad Hakhimi Ahmad Shukri.bio: Kimi is one of Malaysia's SSL pioneers, achieving a notable 10th-place finish in Gran Canaria in 2023. He formerly competed on the World Match Racing Tour (WMRT) as the trimmer for Malaysia's Koo Racing Team (KRT), which reached a world ranking of 13th in November 2016 (World Sailing).|A dominant figure in dinghy sailing, Kimi was national champion for eight consecutive years—first in the International 420 class (2003–2006) and then in the International 470 class (2007–2010). He also represented Malaysia at the Asian Games and the Southeast Asian Games.|Beyond dinghies, Kimi is an active keelboat sailor, competing in the J70, SB20, and various other keelboat classes.|Kimi hails from the state of Penang.
res: World Match Racing Tour Oakcliff International
World Match Racing Tour Oakcliff International

MAS|Asmawi Azman.bio: Asmawi is an ILCA 6 sailor whose journey began as a true “jaguh kampung” a hometown standout who dreamed far beyond familiar shores. Shaped by early experiences in the Plato and J/80 classes, he developed the strong technical foundation and teamwork-driven mindset that continue to define his sailing today. Calm under pressure and deeply connected to the sea, Asmawi now serves in the Royal Malaysian Navy while pursuing excellence on the international stage. In 2025, he will represent Malaysia at the SEA Games in Thailand, testing his skills against the region’s best and proving that determination can carry a sailor from local waters to the world arena. Awie hails from Kuala Terengganu in the state of Terengganu
res: Platu Macth Racing, Royal Selangor Yacht Club.

MAS|Asri Azman.bio: Asri represented Malaysia in the 2014 Youth Olympic Games (Byte Cii), Youth Sailing World Championships (Laser Radial), and the Asian Sailing Championship (Laser Standard). He is a silver medallist in the Southeast Asian (SEA) Games in Laser Standard. He is currently a national dinghy coach. Asri hails from the state of Terengganu.

MAS|Juni Karimah Noor Jamali.bio: Juni competes in the International 470 Mixed class. She began sailing at the age of 14 in the International 420 class as a crew member. In 2019, she transitioned to the International 470 class, continuing as crew alongside her helm, Nur Aisyah Jamil, until 2022. Since then, she has been competing in the 470 Mixed class with a new partner. Together with her former teammate Nur Aisyah Jamil, Juni made history for Malaysia at the Tokyo 2020 Olympic Games by becoming the nation’s first double-handed sailing team to qualify for the Olympics. She is also Malaysia’s youngest sailing Olympian. Juni hails from Langkawi, in the state of Kedah.

MAS|Khairulnizam Mohd Afendy.bio: A Laser Standard sailor, Khairulnizam is a veteran of 4 Olympic Games (London, Rio, Tokyo and Paris). He is a double silver medalist in the Asian Games and a multiple gold medalist in the Southeast Asian Games. He is a regular crew member of top keelboat programs in the Asia Pacific region such as Australia's TP52 Team Hollywood and more recently Thailand's TP52 THA72. He also races in the J70, Fareast 28R and Platu 25 one-design classes in Asia. he continuosly showed a tremendous result by finishing 10th in Gran Canaria SSL World cup and will set sails for up ciming SEA games in Thailand. Nizam hails from Klang in the state of Selangor.

MAS|Khairunnisa Mohd Afendy.bio: She began sailing in the Optimist class, competing in both the Optimist World and Asian Championships, before moving into the 420 and 470 classes. A double-handed helm, she went on to win an Asian Games silver medal and a SEA Games bronze medal, Asian Sailing gold Medal, place 7th at the Volvo 420 Worlds, and 10th at the 470 Junior Worlds. She has also raced in keelboat with the TP52 VAYU and the Farr40 The Next Factor. Now a flight attendant with Malaysia Airlines, she still carries Malaysia’s flag with pride balancing her aviation career with her unwavering passion for sailing and representing her country. Khairunnisa hails from Klang in the state of Selangor.

MAS|Mohamad Faizal Norizan.bio: Faizal won a gold medal in the Asian Games at the age of 18 and is a multiple gold medalist in the Sea Games. He has an unbeaten record in International 420 and 470 in Malaysia. Faizal and his International 420 teammate Ahmad Syukri Abdul Aziz won gold in the 16th Asian Sailing Championships in Korea in 2014 and came second in the ISAF Youth Sailing World Championships in Portugal later in the same year. Faizal also hails from Klang, Malaysia.

MAS|Mohd Akiyuddin Mat ZakI.bio: A former national Laser Standard sailor, Akiyuddin has competed in the Youth Sailing World Championships and the Southeast Asian (SEA) Games. He currently serves in the Royal Malaysian Navy and is a senior member of its keelboat program. With the Navy, he has competed in regattas across Asia in Farr 520, DK47 and Platu 25. Akiyuddin hails from Tanah Merah in the state of Kelantan.

MAS|Mohd Azhar Sadon Zubir.bio: Wak has skippered the Malaysian Armed Forces team's Farr 520 Zuhal. He has competed in regattas across Asia in TP52, Farr 520 and DK47. He is currently head coach of the Malaysian Armed Forces Sailing Team. Wak hails from Muar in the state of Johor.

MAS|Mohd Saifullah Mohd Esa.bio: Saifullah competed in the World Match Racing Tour (WMRT) as bowman on Malaysia's Koo Racing Team (KRT). Their best ranking was 13th in the world (World Sailing Novermber 2016). Saifullah also competed in the WMRT M32 series. More recently he has been competing in the SB20 one-design class in Asia. He hails from Kuala Terengganu in the state of Terengganu.

MYA|Aung Myin Thu.bio: I began sailing in 1994 with the Optimist Class. After completing that stage, I continued sailing in various classes including the Laser II Class, International 420 Class, Enterprise Class, and International 470 Class. Currently, I serve as the Assistant Head Coach at the Myanmar Yachting Federation and as the Sailing Secretary at the Yangon Sailing Club.

MYA|Khin Nyo Lynn.bio: I started practicing sailing in 2005.From 2005 to 2013, I competed in the Int’L 420,470, Laser and windsurfing classes. Since 2013, I have worked as a coach at the Myanmar Yachting Federation. Currently, I have the opportunity to participate as an athlete in the SSL Team.

MYA|Min Min.bio: I began sailing in 2005 with the Int'l 420 Class. After completing that stage, I continued sailing in International 470 Class. Currently, I serve as the Coach at the Myanmar Yachting Federation and as the Asst. Sailing Secretary at the Yangon Sailing Club.

MYA|Min Thaw Kaung.bio: I’m Min Thaw Kaung, and sailing has been a major part of my life. I started sailing the Optimist at age nine and represented my country at the SEA Games when I was thirteen. Later, I moved into the 470 class, sailing with my teammate and gaining valuable racing experience.

MYA|Nan Kham Say.bio: Former National Badminton player before sailing. Started learning sailing in 2001 in 420 class. Then retired from sailing in 2004 and come back again in 2009. And sailed for the National Sailing Team in 2013.

MYA|Sai Pyae Sone Hein.bio: Started sports in middle school as school selection for Badminton and volleyball. But I stopped the other sports and started learning sailing after high school. I have been sailing several Dinghy classes. Currently serves as Captain of Boats of Yangon Sailing Club and the Head Coach of the Myanmar Yachting Federation. I am married to Nang Kham Say and have two sons, 10 and 14 years old.

MYA|Saw Thaw Thi Htoo.bio: I started sailing with the Optimist class in 2013. Following that, I sailed the International 420, the Laser, and the International 470. I competed in the SEA Games with the International 420 and also took up windsurfing. Currently, I am serving as an Assistant Coach at the Myanmar Yachting Federation.

MYA|Sithu Hein.bio: I began sailing in 2016 with the Optimist class and later transitioned into the ILCA as I advanced in the sport. Each step on the water has shaped my racing style, pushing me to grow, adapt, and keep elevating my performance.

MYA|Sithu Moe Myint.bio: 1 of first 4 sailors to start sailing the Optimist in Myanmar when it was first introduced to the country in 1992 and have loved the sport ever since. Currently serves as Commodore of Yangon Sailing Club (founded in 1924) which remains my second home. Apart from sailing, love riding big bikes mainly doing adventure/enduro rides. Lives with 2 Pomeranians whom believed they adopted me and not vice versa.

MYA|Thant Zaw Oo.bio: I started sailing in 2015. I am one of the staff members at the Yangon Sailing Club. I am very happy and excited to be involved in sailing. When I first began, I started sailing with the Sharpie class. I continue to learn and enjoy improving my sailing skills. Sailing is my passion, and I enjoy learning new skills on the water. I participate in club activities and support sailing events.
res: Yangon Sailing Clud Staff Race Championship
Yangon Sailing Clud Staff Race Championship

MYA|Zwe Thura.bio: An experienced dinghy sailor who has represented Myanmar in the IODA Asian Championship and the SEA Games. I have specialized in the Optimist class, gaining extensive competitive experience and developing skills.

NED|Roy Heiner.bio: The captain of SSL Team Netherlands is known for making success possible. Stepping out of the comfort zone, always improving through understanding why, passionate about personal development and team collaboration, because ‘Success is not a coincidence’, it is a choice.

NZL|Chris Main.bio: Chris Main is a New Zealand sailor whose career began in the country’s celebrated P Class, where he won the National Championship in 1990. That early success launched a professional sailing career that included three America’s Cup campaigns, most notably with Japan’s Nippon Challenge in 2000 and Britain’s GBR Challenge in 2003, where he served as a tune-up helmsman and helped develop the team’s training programme. Known for his tactical skill and match-racing experience, Main remained active in elite sailing well beyond the Cup, including campaigns aboard the super maxi CQS. Today, he is a semi-retired farmer in New Zealand, having traded the pressure of grand-prix racing for life on the land.

NZL|Leslie Egnot.bio: Leslie Egnot started sailing in Christchurch New Zealand and had an impact on sailing at a young age. She was the first female to win New Zealands prestigeous Tauranga Cup, sailed in the class unique to NZ - the P Class. At the time, it was the most competitive junior fleet in the country. Egnot progressed to the 470 class where she won a Silver medal sailing with Jan Shearer at the 1992 Olympic Games and has competed in two Americas' Cups. She is the first women to have skippered / helmed an Americas Cup yacht. She has worked for Yachting New Zealand in a variety of roles including high performance coach, logistics manager, an Olympic selector and a member of the Olympic Committee.

NZL|Nick Egnot Johnson.bio: Nick Egnot-Johnson comes from a strong dinghy sailing background, having had great success in the Optimist, Starling and 29er classes. He discovered match racing in 2018 and since then has had a long string of great achievements with his KNOTS Racing Team. He and his team are current World Match Racing Champioins (2023) and have just finished 3rd in the prestigeous Congressional Cup. He holds multiple Match Racing and Keelboat National New Zealand titles. He and his team are currently ranked the 3rd best match racing team in the world, reaching a career best of 2nd in the world. In his spare time Nick has been sailing on various boats, including the foiling moth, TP52's and Melges 40's.

NZL|Robbie McCutcheon.bio: Robbie McCutcheon Started sailing at Wakatere Boating Club at age 7, sailing Optimists, P Class, Starling, 29er and 420. Since then he has been sailing at the highest level nationally and internationally, representing NZ on numerous occasions, Currently Robbie is sailing on the Beau Geste TP52 programboth as a sailor and shore team; competing in IRC and ORC events in Europe. Robbie is also the skipper of his match racing team competing in World Match Race Tour events in Europe and the US.

OMA|Ali Al Balushi.bio: A member of the first ever all-Omani offshore racing team, former footballer Ali Al Balushi made the switch to sailing and has realised his dreams of representing his country. He has already tasted victory as part of the triumphant Team EFG Bank in the 2020 Sailing Arabia – The Tour, held in Oman. Ali has also been part of Oman’s successful MOD70 and M34 squads, setting records and learning from the best in the sport.

OMA|Hussain Al Jabri.bio: Born in the coastal village of Yiti, Hussain Al Jabri’s ascent to the top has been rapid. After just one year as a sailor, he won gold at the Singapore Laser championships, quickly following this up with victory in the Laser Standard Class at the prestigious Sail the Gulf regatta. Known for his hard work, determination and intelligence, Al Jabri is ready for a new challenge in the SSL.

OMA|Nasser Al Maashari.bio: Built like a wrestler and a former international swimmer, Nasser Al Mashari is one of Oman’s most experienced and decorated active sailors. Joining Oman Sail in 2009, he has gained extensive experience in inshore and offshore pursuits, including winning the Extreme Sailing Series for Team Oman Air and taking part in the Tour de France a la Voile. Growing up in a fishing village he was destined to live life on the water, first representing Oman in swimming competitions throughout the Gulf including the Arab Championship in Jordan and World Youth Games in Moscow in 1998.

PER|Alonso Collantes.bio: The first ranked Peruvian on the SSL rankings. He has also been awarded the (Laureles Deportivos del Perú” on one occasion for winning the 2016 and 2017 Sunfish World Championship in Cartagena, Colombia, and New Jersey, USA. He started sailing an Optimist at the age of six. In 2009 he won the individual and Team Racing Optimist South American Championship; it was the first of his three Optimist Team Racing South American Titles. In 2009 and 2011 he finished 2nd at the Optimist Team Racing World Championship. In 2015 he was part of the Peruvian Panamerican Games team. Besides his two Sunfish world championships, he has a 2nd, a 3rd, and a youth world championship title in that class. In 2012 when he was 15 years old, he competed in the Laser class South American Championship in Buenos Aires, Argentina, and achieved a 2nd place overall and 1st U18 in the 4.7 class.

PER|Augusto Nicolini.bio: Augusto is one of Peru’s best all-around sailors. After his career in youth sailing he moved on to Olympic sailing in order to complete his dream of sailing in the Olympic Games. He won a Gold medal at the Bolivarian Games in 2001 and 5 Laser National Championships in 01, 02, 04, 05, and 2010. He reached his goal in 2004 when he participated in the 2004 Olympics. He has been sailing professionally for several years on the J24, J70, Soto 40, and ORC classes. He has achieved multiple national championships in big boat racing in the previously mentioned classes. Since 2007 to this date, he has been the North Sails Manager for Peru.

PER|Christian Sas.bio: Se inicio en la vela a los 13 años en el optimist, para luego participar en Lightning, Laser, J/24, J/70 y veleros Oceánicos, habiendo logrado 17 campeonatos nacionales entre Optimist, Lightning, J/24 y Veleros Oceanicos, asi como un subcampeonato mundial de J/24 (Buenos Aires 2011), asi como haber participado en diversos campeonatos internacionales, mundiales y en 3 juegos panamericanos en J/24, asi como 2 finales de ISAF Nations Cup representando al Perú. Aparte de su experiencia como velerista ha sido entrenador de Optimist por 8 años, tanto de clubes locales, así como de la selección Peruana, ayudando al equipo peruano a obtener distintos logros a nivel internacional. Fue parte del equipo que logro la clasificacion a la SSL Gold Cup.

PER|Eduardo Cano.bio: He has been a sailor since the age of 9, starting with Optimist. Later, he transitioned to windsurfing/J24 and surfing. At a very young age, 17 years old, he began coaching the Peruvian team for many years, which led him to migrate to Mexico to coach the Mexican Optimist team. Some years ago, he reintegrated into competitive sailing, primarily in the windsurfing and J70 classes.

PER|Florencia Chiarella.bio: Florencia was born and raised in Lima, Peru. She started sailing at eight years old on a sailboat called Optimist. Since then, Florencia has represented her club (Club Regatas Lima) and home country (Peru) in multiple national and international championships. In 2017, she became the first woman to win an Optimist South American Championship in Paraguay. The year after (2018), she led the Peruvian national team and championed again in the Team Race Championship. After closing a successful cycle on the Optimist, together with one of her former Optimist colleagues, she started sailing a new boat called Nacra 15. Following Nacra 15, she started competing in the most sailed boat globally, the ILCA, which she continues practicing until this day. In 2021, Florencia won the Youth Sailing World Championship in ILCA 6. Nowadays, she continues training and competing to accomplish her goals.

PER|Ismael Muelle.bio: He started sailing at the age of 8 in the Optimist class and later in the Sunfish and Snipe classes. As a helmsman, he has participated in some world championships, several South American championships and the Pan American Games in Lima 2019. Most of his career as a sailor has been in the Snipe class, where he has been national champion twice. He is currently venturing as a crew member in the ORC class of his country.

PER|Javier Arribas Harten.bio: He started sailing in the Optimist class at the age of five, growing up in a highly competitive fleet alongside his future captain, bowman, grinder, and floater. He managed to achieve several podium finishes in national and international competitions. He has represented his country in almost every class sailed in Peru, winning the Snipe title at the “Bolivariano de Playa,” as well as representing his country at the Pan American Games and campaigning for the Olympics in the Nacra 17 MK2. He currently sails in the Kitefoil and ORC classes, serving as the main trimmer.
res: 2011 IODA Optimist Team Racing World Championship

POL|Igor Tarasiuk.bio: Born in 1997, currently representing Yacht Club Gdansk in the national sailing league and sailing champions league. Involved in many match racing campaigns as a skipper.

POL|Jakub Surowiec.bio: Match Racing World Champion in 2002, part of the top-ranked Match Racing Team for 2 years (2002-2004).As the trimmer along with the Chinese team for the 32 Americas Cup. In total 16 times World Champion, 3 times European champion, and 12 times Polish Champion in various classes.from connection of high-level sailing and unique abilities, I make unique boat models - www.yacht-models.pl

POL|Mateusz Kusznierewicz.bio: Mateusz won the first ever Olympic medal in the history of Polish sailing and together he has two Olympic medals: Gold from Atlanta and Bronze from Athens. He is a four-time World Champion, European Champion in OK-Dinghy, Finn, Star and 5.5 class, as well as a podium winner in the most prestigious regattas in the world: Star Sailors League, Princess Sophia Trophy, Kieler Woche, Bacardi Cup, Palma Vela and many more

POL|Tymoteusz Bendyk.bio: Born in 1990, spend most of his sailing career on high performance catamarans and foiling boats (A-class, F18, 49er, Nacra 17, Moth). Has a Master degree in Applied physics. Lot of experience in technical part of high performance sailing.

POR|Afonso Domingos.bio: He is the first European to win the Bacardi Cup, one of the oldest and more traditional sailing events, in 2004 and again in 2008. He sailed in 3 Olympic Games, Sydney, Beijing and London in two different classes, the 49er and the Star. Has won 2 diplomas, one in each class and his best ISAF ranking was the 2nd at the 49er and the 4th on the Star. The CEO and Skipper of the best international Portuguese team, a Sailboat of the Class Soto40, the Bigamist. Nowadays Afonso keeps sailing in every kind of boats. For instance keel boats, on the class ORC to J70. On the first one he achieved the title of World Champion in 2022 and in 2021. And on the second he missed the Podium by just one point in the World Championship in this last year. He also coached many different boats, like the 49er, Sniper, keel boats... and has results such as the 3rd place on the World Championship of Snipe in 2022 and the 2nd place on the European Championship of 6M in 2022.

POR|Filipe Silva.bio: Filipe was born in Lisbon and started sailing in Algarve at the age of 6 in the optimist class. He represented Portugal in the World Championship when he was 13. Since then, he has achieved two bronze medals, four silver medals and two gold medals in Worlds and Europeans Championships, in different classes. He lives in Algarve and still has a passion for sailing, competing worldwide in the finn class and many other classes.

POR|Hugo Rocha.bio: One of the most recognized and famous Portuguese sailors, both for his passion for the sport and for his results.|Hugo Rocha competed in 3 Olympic Games. Winning a Medal in the 470 Class, in Atlanta. He still conquered 9 World Championships in the most diverse classes, from Laser II, Platu 25, J80, SB20, Swan 45 to ORC class, and he is also 5 times European Champion. In 2023, he participated for the first time in an Oceanic race, the Ocean Race, with a 100% Portuguese crew, the Mirpuri Foundation Racing Team and after this experience he even got closer to the Ocean and improved his skills.

POR|João Rodrigues.bio: João was born in the Pearl of the Atlantic, Madeira Island and has been a successful windsurfer since the late nineties. Has competed in 7 Olympic Games, with 3 World Titles and 5 European Titles in different Windsurfing Classes, he is the Captain of the Portuguese Team. His Experience on and off the water, will help the team to thrive, giving them the confidence to perform at their best.

POR|Mariana Lobato.bio: Mariana started Sailing at the age of seven, in Optimist Class and was born in the Capital of Portugal, Lisbon. She was representing Portugal in the Olympic Games in London, 2012 in the Match Racing class and achieved the title of World Champion in Korea in 2013!|She also sails in large boats in several teams which helped her gain a lot of experience. After being a mother of two, she achieved the victory in the Ocean Race Europe of 2021 and finished 4th in the Ocean Race of 2023, aboard of the French Team, Biotherm in the IMOCA Class. For her, the opportunity to learn every day with the other team members is always an asset and the Teamwork is undoubtedly the most interesting challenge on board.
res: ISAF Women's Match Racing World Championship

POR|Nuno Miguel Santos Barreto.bio: Nuno was born in Lisbon, is one of the sailors of the Golden Generation of the Portuguese sailing. He has a Bronze Medal in the Olympic Games in Atlanta 1996 on the 470 class and has participated in Two other Olympic Games. In the America's Cup, he was part of the Spanish Challenge of 2007 and accumulated 3 World Titles, has 5 Medals in the Europeans and 15 years of Professional Circuits always Trimming Genoas and Spis. On top of this Experience, Nuno is a good Comunicator and has a lot of Experience so it is Excellent to have him on board, especially if you want to have the boat Sailing at his Optimal Conditions.

POR|Paulo Manso.bio: Another sailor on our team who was born in the Pearl of the Atlantic... Madeira Island. Paulo Manso was involved with Nature and the Sea from a very early age. When he started to take his first steps in sailing, at just 7 years old, he immediately felt a passion for this sport. He sails until today and competes on several circuits.

RSA|Howard Leoto.bio: Howard is a small business owner from Masiphumelele near Cape Town. He started boating in 2004 at the Izivunguvungu school in Simon's Town. He currently uses Laser Radial and 420 boats and has won two national events.

RSA|Ian Ainslie.bio: He was born on July 27, 1965, in Johannesburg, South Africa, and started sailing at the age of 12. Ian Ainslie is a three-time Olympian in the Finn Class. He started the Izivunguvungu school for transforming sailing in South Africa and was a head coach of the Netherland Olympic sailing team in London 2012 and Rio 2016

RSA|Joweal Klaase.bio: Joweal is the bowman who has won the most Lipton cup regattas, the most prestigious regatta in South Africa. He is employed in a sail design office. He is also an alumnus of Izivunguvungu. He was introduced to the sport at the age of 15 by a sailing school called (Izivunguvungu) founded by Ian Ainslie and Matthew Mentz.

RSA|Marco Tobin.bio: He was born in Cape Town, South Africa, and started sailing at the age of 13. Marco actively takes part in multiple dinghy and keel boat fleets within National and International events. He`s currently the director of Zeekoevlei Sailing Centre which introduces school for transforming sailing in South Africa and is the Head of Claims Operations for Metropolitan Health.

RSA|Mark Sadler.bio: Mark grew up in Benoni, near Johannesburg. he won just about every title in south africa in dinghies and small keelboats, including a j22 worlds.he was the skipper of the south african america's cup team shosholoza. he currently lives in palma de mallorca where he forms part of the management of the north sails loft. he competes professionally on a vast array of keelboats from swan 50's to super yachts.

SEY|Allan Julie.bio: My name is Allan julie. and I am from of the Seychelles. I am a passionate and dedicated sailor, currently serving as the captain of the Seychelles SSL Gold Club Team. Throughout my sporting career, I have had the honor of representing my country at seven Olympic Games, a journey that has been one of the greatest achievements of my life. Over the years, I have also won several medals at African Championships and have been recognized as Seychelles' Best Sportsman on seven occasions. These accomplishments reflect my commitment, perseverance, and love for sport. Sailing has been a major part of my life for more than 20 years. Today, I continue to enjoy the sport by racing a FarEast 28 yacht with my friends. We participate in many weekend regattas and enjoy the camaraderie and excitement that sailing brings. Beyond competitive sailing, I have a strong interest in windsurfing and canoeing, both of which allow me to stay connected to the ocean and maintain an active lifestyle.
