In my free time, I enjoy playing dominoes with friends at the beach near my home. The friendly competition and social atmosphere make it one of my favorite ways to relax. Looking back on my journey, I am proud of what I have achieved in sport and grateful for the opportunities I have had to represent Seychelles on the international stage. My passion for sailing remains as strong as ever, and I continue to embrace new challenges both on and off the water.

SEY|Brian Tousaint.bio: My name is Brian Toussaint, and I am 46 years old from Seychelles. I started sailing at the age of 8 and developed a passion for the sea from a very young age. At the age of 12, I discovered windsurfing, which became another important part of my sporting journey. Over the years, I have represented Seychelles in numerous national, regional, and international windsurfing competitions. My professional career has been equally diverse. I worked on cruise ships, later joined the Seychelles Coast Guard, and today I work as a VIP Driver with Creole Travel Services, where I have the privilege of helping visitors discover the beauty, culture, and unique experiences that Seychelles has to offer. In my spare time, I continue to stay actively involved in sailing through training sessions on the Fareast 28 yacht. Being on the water remains one of my greatest passions and a constant source of motivation. Today, I am proud and excited to be part of the Seychelles SSL Gold Club Team. I look forward to contributing my experience, learning from my teammates, and helping showcase Seychellois sailing on the international stage.

SEY|Curtis Allcorn.bio: Growing up as an expat, having lived in multiple countries, Bahrain, Botswana, St Lucia, Turks and Caicos, England, to name a few, but always periodically returning home to the Seychelles, I was always ready to settle down and truly enjoy my home islands, and after 15 years in the UAE, I did just that and bought a racing yacht.Sailing in the tropical paradise of the Seychelles, warm water and breezes, blue skies, green islands is hard to beat. I have always been enamored with the sea, a competitive sports man and an environmentalist, sailing manages to tick all the boxes for me.

SEY|Eston Dubel.bio: Hi my name eston dubel i'm seychellois sailor at the age of 13 sailing instructor windsurfing instructor now doing sail repair work sail far east 28 won manny natoinals during my younger days still enjoying a good breeze and verry happy to be in the SLL gold cup team representing sechelles.By the way i was one of first among 4 seychellois to teach sailing for the first time in my country and i'm very proud to see how far we've been thanks

SEY|Jayden Vidot.bio: I started sailing at 8 years old. From which the ocean became my playground. I do most of the water sports you can think of, sailing, surfing, windsurfing, kiting, diving and fishing. Throughout my sailing career, I’ve represented Seychelles in national and regional events in the ilca class, winning regional championships and being national champion twice. I have also done some European training events, mainly in Valencia. I have since moved on from ilca sailing and now skippering a keel boat in the fareast 28r fleet. Now currently sailing the ssl 47 boat, I’m excited to see what the future holds for my team in yacht sailing.

SEY|Joshua Allcorn.bio: Im Joshua Allcorn, a Seychellois sailor and multi sport national athlete. I’ve picked up many sports throughout my life, and I picked up sailing at 13, moving my way from Optimist to ILCA to skipper on a FarEast 28, winning national and regional championships. My life has revolved around the water and the tropics, exploring Seychelles’ reefs, islands and forests, while travelling to other countries through any sport I can compete my way into. When there’s wind, I sail/ kitesurf. Waves, I boggieboard. Clear water, I dive. Rain, I hike to find waterfalls, and of course, photograph as much of it as I can. BJJ, swimming, and sailing have taken me to many countries, and my goal is to help more people discover these sports and make our presence in international competitions much more pronounced.

SEY|Marcus Ahweng.bio: I’m quite new to sailing, I started towards the end of last year, but being surronded by so many great sailors on the team has taught me so much, so fast. I love learning new things and trying out new challenges. I think time is valuable, and learning as many new skills as possible is one of the best ways to live. A few of my favourite hobbies include surfing, fishing and free diving, as I love all things to do with water. I also enjoy photography, hiking and essentially anything to do with nature because it is a true gift. A very recent hobby of mine has been jogging and I’ve really loved training for and competing in my first marathon. But something that has really fueled me is my passion for health, whether it be health of the mind or of the body. I hope to continue sailing because it is such a beautifully composed sport and really teaches a lot: I especially love the way we humans learn to flow with nature through this athletic form of art.

SGP|Jovina Choo.bio: The captain of SSL Team Singapore has participated in some of the biggest events in sailing – and will soon add the SSL Gold Cup to her impressive resume. In a career spanning over 20 years, Jovina has finished top 3 in over 30 Optimist, 420, 470 and keelboat competitions at the national, regional and international level. Her most recent achievement was clinching the gold medal with the Singapore keelboat team at the Saemangeum Cup International Regatta in Korea. A natural-born leader, Jovina has been the captain of numerous school and national teams, and holds the key to charting the future of Singapore keelboat sailing.

SGP|Ryan Lo.bio: Introduced to Sailing from the age of 7, Ryan has had a most illustrious sailing career. Currently campaigning for this year's Asian Games, Ryan is no stranger to competitions on the world stage, with his latest achievement being a 10th-place finish in a fleet of 163 ILCA 7 dinghies at the prestigious Princess Sofea Regatta 2022, held in Mallorca. Growing up, Ryan started amassing his medals from a young age, with a SEA Games bronze medal at the age of 13 and an Optimist Team Racing Gold at the World Championships (NZL) the year after. The transition to the ILCA (then Laser) class was a natural one, with some of his career highlights:|1. 2014 ISAF Youth Worlds, Laser 4.7: Bronze 2. 2017 & 2019 SEA Games, Laser Standard: Gold 3. 2018 Asian Games, Laser Standard: Bronze 4. 2020 Summer Olympics, ILCA 7: 21 / 35 In his limited free time, Ryan enjoys Cycling, Tennis & Golf. Fun Fact, siblings Jun Hao and Man Yi are also accomplished sailors, having sailed for Singapore on the international stage as well.
res: Mussanah Open Championship 2021- Asian and African OG Qualifier Mussanah Open Championship 2021- Asian and African OG Qualifier
2011 IODA Optimist Team Racing World Championship

SGP|Terena Lam.bio: Terena started sailing in 2011 and trained as a bowman since then. She has competed in many keelboat classes and events, including regular podium finishes at the Singapore Straits Regatta, Top of the Gulf Regatta, J24 National Champs, and RSYC Regatta. She was also a 5th place finisher at the World University Match Race Championships.
res: South East Asian Games Fleet Race,

SUI|Eric Monnin.bio: Self-made talent and allrounder, the Captain of SSL Team Switzerland has climbed up the Match Racing world rankings to become number one, and has three times been crowned European Champion. After getting into sailing competition on the Surprise yacht of the family, Eric Monnin sailed in many monohull classes, including winning the Platu 25 World Championship, as well as on the D35 catamaran fleet on Lake Geneva, twice winning the Bol d’Or.
res: EUROSAF Match Race - Open European Championship 2019
Match Race Germany - World Match Racing Tour 2015
Argo Group Gold Cup - Alpari World Match Racing Tour 2014

SUI|Kilian Wagen.bio: Kilian started sailing at the age of 6 in Optimist class, then moved on to Laser 4.7, 420, and finally to the 470 class where he campaigned for the Tokyo 2020 Olympics but unfortunately did not qualify. He is currently undergoing an apprenticeship as a master sailor. He is the reigning J70 world champion.

TAH|Hervé Cunningham.bio: Né à Tahiti, Hervé Cunningham a commencé la voile à l’âge de six ans, en pratiquant à la fois l’Optimist et la voile en quillard. Naviguer aux côtés de certaines légendes de la voile tahitienne lui a permis de développer ses compétences et d’approfondir sa connaissance du sport. À 16 ans, il est retourné en France, où il s’est lancé dans le Match Racing, la course au large sur de grands voiliers et la navigation en multicoques. Tout au long de sa carrière de navigateur professionnel, il a participé à des compétitions côtières et hauturières, acquérant une solide expérience dans de nombreuses classes de bateaux.

TAH|Manoarii Plichart.bio: Born in Tahiti, Manoarii Plichart began his sailing journey in the Optimist class before spending four years in France. He then joined the Pôle Espoir in La Rochelle, where he sailed the Nacra 15. He now competes in the ILCA 7 class, continuing to develop his skills and experience in competitive sailing.

TAH|Manutea Mahai.bio: A professional fisherman, Manutea discovered sailing in 2016. He sails alongside Teva in Diam24. He was vice-champion of France in Diam24 in 2017 and 2nd in the Tour Voile the same year.

TAH|Moana Hugonot.bio: A Life Dedicated to the Ocean Moana’s maritime journey began in 1987 aboard the famous training ship La Fleur de Lampaul, a foundational experience that defined his life's path. In 1989, he entered the fishing school at Île d'Yeu, gaining his first open-ocean experience on tuna trollers. Returning to Tahiti in 1993, he initially worked as a deckhand on new longliners arriving from Concarneau, crisscrossing every corner of Polynesia (Marquises, Tuamotu, Gambier, Australes) as well as the Cook and Kiribati islands. In 1996, he completed his military service in the French Navy aboard the patrol vessel La Tapageuse, a deployment that expanded his horizons to the Tonga and Niue islands. Following these diverse experiences, his leadership led him to become a captain from 2001 to 2017, commanding various tuna vessels ranging from 15 to 25 meters. In 2017, Moana chose to transition his career, leaving commercial longline fishing in 2019 to bring his extensive expertise to the yachting industry. Relying on his vast sea time, he officially validated his skills in 2022, earning his Master 200 and Master 200 Sail captain's certificates along with all required safety modules. As a highly qualified skipper, he has mastered a wide variety of catamarans, including various Lagoon models (620, 43, 42, 40), Fountaine-Pajot yachts (Saba 50, Isla 40, Lucia 40, Tana 47), as well as the Excess 11. Now based in Raiatea for the past three years, where he lives aboard, he initially worked with TradeWinds, catering to a predominantly American clientele. Today, he operates as a freelance professional skipper for Tahiti Yacht Charter. Highly trusted by his clients, he is currently completing a trans-Pacific delivery from Panama. This latest catamaran project was born from a partnership with a former client and investor, alongside Teva Pichard. Together, they are also preparing to represent Tahiti in the upcoming SSL Gold Cup qualifiers in Switzerland, where Moana will serve as a trimmer. A devoted solo father to his two children, Kealohilani and Keahi, Moana beautifully combines a unique lifetime of maritime expertise, family devotion, and an unwavering passion for the seafaring life.

TAH|Teiki Hacheche.bio: Teiki learned sailing with his oncles (hobie cat world champion) at 7 years old, and turned into optimist contest quickly, than multihull. Now his is profesional skipper in French Polynesia on boats from 40 to 65 feet

TAH|Teriimana Degage.bio: Teriimana Degage a commencé la voile en 2016 à bord d’une pirogue Holopuni. Il a participé à sa première compétition lors de l’événement test de la SSL en 2021, où il occupait le poste de grinder. Aujourd’hui, il est moniteur de va’a, la pirogue à balancier emblématique de Tahiti, et transmet sa passion pour ce sport nautique traditionnel.

TAH|Teva Plichart.bio: After racing the Hobbie Cat in Tahiti, Teva joined Match-Racing France's Youth team. He then raced with Paolo Cian winning European Championship. In 2007, he skippered “Tahiti Tourisme” reaching Tour de France à la Voile's 2nd place. He renewed the result 10 years later with “Treasures of Tahiti”. From 2016 until 2019, he sailed on Yliam Comptoir Immobilier winning the famous 2019 Bol d'Or in the D35 category. He continues to race with the same team on TF35.
res: ISAF Nations Cup Regional Final – Oceania,

TAH|Tom Lamotte.bio: Tom is from the same generation as Caesar. He was also his teammate in a Hobie Cat in Tahiti. Now at the Mediterranean Training Center (CEM) in La Grande Motte, he is one of the hopes of French sailing in Nacra17.

THA|Anusorn Ngamrit.bio: Anusorn started sailing at the age of 10 under the guidance of his father. He began with the optimist sailboat in the youth category of Thailand, JSST selected him to represent Thailand in the ASEAN Optimist Championship 2008. He then moved on to the ILCA 4.7 and was selected to participate in the ILCA 4.7 Youth World Championship 2010. As he grew older, he transitioned to the 420 and later the 470. Although he started as a helmsman, he became a crew competing in various classes in national competitions for the 470, Nacra15, Hobie16, Nacra17, F18, F20, 29er, Platu25, Fareast26, Fareast28R, Swan31, Swan42, RC44, TP52.

THA|Chusit Punjamala.bio: Pop started sailing at 8 after his primary school added sailing into the course which was mandatory for all 4th graders to complete. He found sailing so enjoyable and peaceful until that one day he capsized in the storm during his second regatta of his life and scared himself so badly he wanted to quit, however, his mum encouraged him to overcome his fears and keep sailing. By 10 he became part of the Optimist national team and later in the ILCA where he has been pursuing his Olympic dream as a frequent gold fleet sailor at world championships. Nowadays, Pop coaches aspiring sailors and passes on his in depth knowledge when he isn't practicing his swings on the gold course.

THA|Don Whitcraft.bio: Don started sailing at the age of 5 after his parents insisted and scared him just the right amount to keep sailing. Once he was 10, he was hooked on racing. Being in the same generation as our best Opti team ever, he learnt a lot from chasing behind Nai. After taking a break to focus on his studies, he has been campaigning for the 49ers with his brother Dylan. Don is super excited to get the opportunity to race against some of the best sailors ever. Besides sailing, Don enjoys chess and exploring the world through google earth.

THA|Dylan Whitcraft.bio: With a background in the 49er and Fireballs, Dylan races competitively in the TP52, Maxi, and Cape 31 both inshore and offshore. In the rare moments that he isn't sailing, Dylan lives on a Mango farm near Khao Yai National Park, where he cycles and frequently has wild elephants as guests.

THA|Navee Thumpsuntorn.bio: Navee Thamsoontorn, a member of Thailand's national sailing team in the 470 class, is an athlete who thrives on challenges and competition. He has spent most of his life sailing from the moment he first asked his father to let him sail. Through dedication and intensive training, he earned a spot on the national team at the age of 13 and has remained a key member to this day. Over the years, Navee has competed in several classes, starting with the Optimist, then the 420, and now the 470. His ultimate goal is to qualify for the Olympic Games and to continue contributing to the growth and success of Thai sailing in the future.

THA|Nichapa Waiwai.bio: Nay started sailing at the age of 11 after her father pushed her to try it. Although she was initially afraid to get into the sport due to social norms against having dark skin as a girl in Thailand, she overcame her fears and went sailing where she later fell in love with the sport and being on the water. Nay went on to win multiple Asian Games medals in the 29er and 49er FX which forged her reputation as a Thai force majeure. Lately, she has been competing in the mixed 470 and is also an activist for women in sports in Thailand.

THA|Nut Butmarasri.bio: When he was 10 years old, he started sailing during the holiday close to his relative's house on the eastern seaboard. Having been forced to play sports because of his addiction to computer games, he became fascinated with sailing and has been doing this sport ever since.

UKR|Andrii Husenko.bio: Andrii Husenko is a distinguished sailor achieved victory in the 2008 Finn Silver Cup in Hungary and further solidified his legacy as an 11-time National Champion in Ukraine. His remarkable success highlights both his exceptional skill in the Finn class and enduring dominance on the national stage, making him a source of inspiration in competitive sailing.

UKR|Andrii Klochko.bio: Andrii Klochko achieved the SB20 European Championship in 2012, followed by back-to-back SB20 World Championships in 2013 and 2015. Maintaining his winning streak, he secured another SB20 World Championship in 2016. Klochko's remarkable skill and dedication have solidified his reputation as a formidable force in competitive sailing.

UKR|Denis Osliak.bio: Denys Osliak, born on June 2, 1997, is a promising sailor whose career highlights include a 12th position in the 2018 470 World Championship in Bracciano and notable achievements in the L30 category in Marseille, France, in 2020. With a dedication to the sport and demonstrated proficiency, Osliak is emerging as a rising star in the international sailing scene, making him one to watch for future accomplishments.

UKR|Georgiy Paches.bio: Georgiy Paches, born on 1995, is an experienced Ukrainian sailor and main trimmer of the SSL boat. He has achieved notable results, including winning silver at the Youth Laser World Championship and ranking 8th in the Finn Men's event at the Hempel World Cup Series in Miami 2020.

UKR|Ihor Matviienko.bio: Ihor Matvienko, Atlanta 1996 Olympic champion in the 470 class, continued his sailing legacy at the Sydney and Athens Games for Ukraine. Beyond medals, he founded the MIR Yacht Club in Dnipro, passionately promoting sailing among all age groups. Matvienko, now the head of the regional sailing authority, dedicates himself to fostering a love for the sport and nurturing the next generation of sailors in his hometown.

UKR|Oscar Madonich.bio: Oskar Madonich, born in 2003, is a Ukrainian sailor and tactician for the team.One of his recent significant achievement is a silver medal at the 2023 U21 ILCA7 World Championship in Morocco.

UKR|Rodion Luka.bio: During his career, the captain of SSL Team Ukraine has come a long way, from youth classes to steering yachts on the Volvo Ocean Race. Among his achievements are medals from the Olympic Games and gold at the World and European Championships, in the Olympic class. In total, he climbed the world championships podium seven times in different classes of one-designs. A true leader, with experience and high performance in four Olympic Games, will certainly lead the team to the top of the SSL Nations Gold Cup.

UKR|Ruslana Taran.bio: One of the best yachtsmen in the world ever. She became a medalist three times at three Olympic Games in two yacht classes. Four-time winner of gold medals at the World Championship. ISAF ROLEX Yachtswoman of the Year. A true team player in any crew.

URU|Diego Stefani.bio: Experienced bowman and trimmer, “Scrapy” was on board in 2005 when the Memo Memulini obtained the ORC World Championship. Etchells North American champion and two times Southamerican Snipe champion, he also won the Maxi Yacht Rolex Cup in Porto Cervo in 2019 and has raced in the TP52 and GC32 classes, to mention just a few of the wide variety of yachts he has sailed professionally.

URU|Domimique Knüppel.bio: Olympic Sailor in the Nacra 17 class, she obtained the fourth position in the Panamerican Games Lima 2019, securing a spot in the Tokio 2020 Olympics, alongside the skipper Pablo Defazio. There they finished in the 18th position. In World Championships they reached the gold fleet in two occasions, getting the 17th place in 2017 and the 23rd in 2018. She was selected for The Magenta Project 2021 mentoring programme. Knüppel sails in all type of boats and has participated in the Maxi Yacht Rolex Cup onboard Nefertiti (Swan 90) and Moat (Swan 115) as bowwoman. She participates in the offshore Nastro Rosa Tour since 2021, onboard Figaro 3.

URU|Federico Caballero.bio: He sails since he has been 6 years old, when he started in the Optimist class. He then sailed in Laser, Soling and Windsurf. With a vast experience in J24, he was part of National champions crews. Sailing in Soto 40 sin 2009 as a pitman, he was two times winner of the Mitsubishi Cup, in Brazil, and two times national champion in Chile. In Soto 33 he is three times Argentinian champion, and in Soto 50 two times champion in Perú. Recently he participated in three Maxi Yacht Rolex Cup campaigns, onboard Nefertiti (Swan 90) and Moat (Swan 115).

URU|Fernando Díz.bio: He began sailing at nine years old, after he and his brother received a scholarship at the Punta del Este Yacht Club. He took part in two Southamerican and two World Championships in Optimist. Also participated in two Southamerican and one World Championship in Laser. In 2016 he joined Hernán Umpierre to compete in 29er, and after a year and a half -having assisted to one Southamerican and two World Championships-, the shifted to 49er, to begin their Olympic campaign. Together they have been Youth European Champions (U23), overall Asiatic Champions, bronze medalists in the Junior World Championship, and Top 15 in the World Championship.

URU|Hernán Umpierre.bio: He is currently sailing in the 49er class along with Fernando Diz, with whom they are seeking to qualify for the 2024 Olympics. Together they have been Youth European Champions (U23), overall Asiatic Champions, bronze medalists in the Junior World Championship, and Top 15 in the World Championship. Hernán was also Northamerican Optimist Champion, and ended in the 13th position in the Optimist World Championship. He studies Maritime Engineering and Naval Architecture at the University of Cádiz.

USA|Eric Doyle.bio: Star World Champion in 1999 with Tom Olsen, Eric Doyle has been successful in different classes, but the one true love is the Star, where he often finds himself competing directly against Team USA Captain Paul Cayard. Eric was raised in Pass Christian along the Mississippi Gulf Coast, where he learned at a young age that he was hooked on sailing. Vince Brun found him after college, and he began his career at North Sails in 1992. Shortly after that he was hired by Dennis Conner to sail with Stars & Stripes America’s Cup campaign in 2000. Continuing on, he raced with BMW Oracle for the 2003 and 2007 America’s Cup campaigns. Eric’s passion is with smaller keel boats, other than the Star, like the Etchells, Melges 24, and J/70. But he doesn’t shy away from the big boats, winning the Maxi World Championship in 2004. Eric is currently based in San Diego.

USA|Paul Cayard.bio: Paul Cayard is one of the very few sailors who has competed at top level in the three disciplines of the sport: The Olympics, The America’s Cup and Offshore round the world racing. It is impossible to shrink his career to a few lines; with over forty years of experience in sailing, he more than earns his title as a legend of the sport. Cayard has won World Championships in seven different classes. He is a seven-time America's Cup competitor and circumnavigated the world twice, becoming the first American to win the Whitbread Round the World Race in 1998 and placing second with the Disney syndicate Pirates of the Caribbean in the 2005-2006 edition of the Volvo Ocean Race. Cayard is a two-time Olympian (1984, 2004), and he won the Louis Vuitton Cup in 1992 with the Italian syndicate Il Moro di Venezia, becoming one the most appreciated skippers in Italy. Cayard's accolades include induction to the US Sailing Hall of Fame (2011), and the Rolex Yachtsman of the Year Award (1998), he also serves on the Board of US Olympic Sailing. Out of all of this he will be quick to declare that his most treasured prize is winning the Star World Championship in 1988 in Buenos Aires, Argentina.
